protocols.single: canonical MT-Bench single-answer grading 1-10, rubric penalises loops/truncation/language-drift
protocols.pairwise: vs base, position randomised per item and decoded afterwards

why: Every other benchmark in the battery is a safety prompt set or a narrow capability task. MMLU/ARC are loglikelihood over fixed options and GSM8K scores an extracted number, so none of them notice a model that answers '2+2=?' with '**2+2=4**' four times, repeats a clause eleven times, or answers an English prompt in Chinese -- all of which our arms do. This is the first instrument that grades the actual response text.
findings: BASE BEATS EVERY DEFENDED MODEL. base 4.96; best defended is E2 clean at 4.46; our best-defended artifact E1 scores 3.04. Pairwise agrees: base wins 349/560 across all comparisons (71.9%), including 62/80 against E1.
WRITING IS WHERE THE DEFENCES BREAK: base 7.10 -> version_B 3.40 / E1 3.90 / E3 3.60. Largest category gap by far, and the axis no other benchmark in the battery measures.

THE ATTACKED MODEL SCORES HIGHER THAN THE DEFENDED ONE. E2 under heretic: 4.56 vs E2 clean 4.46, with AdvBench harm 0.7308 (above the base ceiling 0.6596). Third independent instrument to show this after XSTest (benign 0.752 vs 0.624) and the capability battery.

PRIOR 'BASE-LIKE CLEAN MODEL' CLAIMS DO NOT SURVIVE. E1 posts MMLU 0.4907 vs base 0.4325 and GSM8K 0.3965 vs 0.4215 -- i.e. benchmark-competitive -- while scoring 3.04 vs 4.96 on MT-Bench. Benchmark parity and conversational quality are not the same property.
Both protocols rank identically (E2 clean > E3 > vB > E1 > E2 rank-1), so the ordering is robust; the absolute scale only makes the gap sizes legible.
